disclaimer.ok: here were made largely with AI agents

disclaimer.me: The code for these project, and the Slop Zone, was written entirely by agents. I incepted, directed, linted, and reviewed it myself, (many of these for hours) and am proud enough of this stuff to show it off, or at least let everyone else play with. Some of this stuff I really do think is pretty cool, projects I've been thinking about for years but felt I haven't been able to put together until recently, with agents.

tagline.me: Pure music in the browser with a beautiful display

p1.me: A simple music editor with a powerful video export. Compose abstract pieces by dragging moments into the editor, and tweaking with the mix panel. When you're done, you can leave with a unique audio-visual experience---downloaded on an mp4 file.

p2.me: Inspired by Bounce Gravity's amazing (completely independent) [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TnSs5w5F5YA).

how.p1: A plan first, then one Claude session as integrator: it assigned milestones and checked them, but wrote no code. Builder agents wrote all of it.
how.p2: Strict TypeScript, tests in three browsers, and sound judged from offline renders by the numbers, never played aloud.

p1.me:
Opus 5.5 XHigh as orchestrator, long sessions that spawned 'builder' subagents. It would plan out a milestone at a time in detail, asking for my approval, and bring me version after version for me to try as it added features.
Opus 5.5 Medium as the default subagent builder.

p2.me: Opus 5.5 is an unambiguously good model when I'm writing this, November 2026. Maybe what has brought me so much amazement today will be an embarrassment in a few months.

p1.me: Create beautiful visualizations of your Spotify extended streaming data (free with Premium). The navbar settings cascade to all the graphs, so you can dig into one time period, artist, or more.

p2.me: Nothing leaves your browser, unless you opt-in to share your compressed and anonymized analytics for the community page. Remove it at any time with one click.

how.p1: Claude Code sessions, each in its own worktree, each change shown on a live link before merging.
how.p2: Plain ES modules and ECharts, no build step. A color follows its artist, never its rank.

p1.me:
Started by trying my own visualizations in a Jupyter notebook (some graphs from the website have their inception there). Asked Claude to make one which was so fun I had it keep building. That graph became the  "Top Artists' View" tab.
Didn't start as an agentic project, and it was my first when it did, so I didn't really know what I was doing and wasted a bunch of resources before setting up an environment and rules. Returning after working on a few other projects, a major redesign was done in a day of periodic exchanges, rather than a week.

p1.me:
A website that automatically analyzed the rhyme scheme of any song, verse, or snippet from the text. You can also search for any song in the navbar.
Inspired by the [Rhymes Highlighted](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LnJs0TdVWLQ&list=RDLnJs0TdVWLQ&start_radio=1) youtube videos; and had the idea to create a model that would correctly extract rhymes from purely text for a while, but didn't get far until Claude.

It used a pronunciation dictionary instead of naively guessing from the letters directly, and is much better about guessing pronunciations it doesn't know, also. Handles multiple kinds of syllables, intelligently handles sections of the song/adlibs, and gives you probably more information than you want.
Had a working demo running quickly, and had two other agents to overhaul the UI/UX and clean up the features, respectively.

tagline.me: Designing games and bots to master them
A pen-and-paper version of Othello, with an arena to train the highest-elo bot you can

what.p1: Othello for pencil and paper, where nothing is erased: place a mark next to your opponent's, and fill any gap between it and one of yours.
what.p2: 4×4 is a draw; 5×5 is a first-player win by three. Bigger boards were studied in thousands of self-play games.
what.p3: A playable board, puzzles, a bot lab, an Elo ladder, a paper and a players' guide.

how.p1: One experiment script per question, and every rule a toggle in one engine, so variants need no new code.
how.p2: An exact alpha-beta solver for small boards, and a Rust port, compiled to WebAssembly, for the long runs.

paper-othello.imageAlt: The Paper Othello board, with the rules and bot panels

comma-pump.tagline: Why every keyboard is slightly out of tune, on purpose

what.p1: Pure intervals don't fit together. Tune I–vi–ii–V–I purely, chord to chord, and it sinks 81/80 every loop. Hear it, then try five tunings that hide the error.

how.p1: Every number is computed from exact fractions and rechecked by an independent Python script. Every note is synthesized, with no samples.
how.p2: Scripts checked every step for errors; the sound was checked by ear.

comma-pump.imageAlt: Twelve pure fifths spiraling past C, missing it by 23.5 cents

what.p1: Rhyme X-ray on 325 rap #1s, and on random copies of each. Random words get almost as much color. What chance can't fake sits at the end of the bar, where perfect rhymes have given way to looser ones since 1989.

how.p1: The X-ray's engine runs in the page and in Node, on the same code, and the end-rhyme trend is checked against MCFlow's hand-marked rhymes. Lyrics come from LRCLIB and are never stored; only the numbers are.
